description.en: The aim of this experiment is to verify Norton's Theorem by determining the Norton current and Norton resistance, then comparing the calculated load current with the observed load current.
The Instructions provide step-by-step guidance on how to perform the simulation.
To use this feature, click on the “AI Guide” button. The AI guide will assist you in performing the simulation accurately at each step.

The CHECK button verifies all the connections to ensure that they are correct.
Note: (a) If a wire is connected incorrectly, click the corresponding label number to remove the connection.
(b) Sources should be switched ON only after the current case connections are verified.
Click AUTO CONNECT to make the required connections for the current Norton measurement stage automatically.
The ADD button adds the readings to the observation table.

The CALCULATE button transfers the measured Norton values to the calculation panel. Enter the Norton current and resistance values, calculate the load current, and use VERIFY to compare it with the observed value.
The RESET button refresh the simulation to its initial state for a fresh start.
The PRINT button allows you to print the simulation.
Set R1, R2, R3, and RL before making the circuit connections. Keep these values unchanged throughout the experiment.
The digital multimeter is used with the supply switched off to measure the Norton resistance seen at the load terminals.

The DC ammeter measures the short-circuit current and the load current during their respective Norton measurement stages.

Rating: 0-10 A DC.

The DC power supply energizes the circuit for the short-circuit-current and load-current measurements. Switch it on only after the connections have been checked.

Rating: 10 V DC.
This section displays the circuit and allows users to make the required connections for each case by dragging and dropping wires between the connection points.
This table records the supply voltage, short-circuit current, Norton resistance, load current, and load resistance used for verification.
This section displays the equations used for the Norton equivalent and load-current calculation.
Use the calculation panel to calculate the load current from the measured Norton current and resistance, then compare it with the observed load current.
After entering the Norton current and resistance values, click VERIFY to compare the calculated load current with the observed load current.
After completing the measurements and verifying the Norton load-current calculation, use this button to generate the experiment report.
